rounds.reasoning_summary:
**Evaluating sampling strategy**

I need to select a stratified sample for auditing. My plan is to focus on all sales over $50k plus a random sample of 30 transactions from both sides of the amount. I'll propose a reasonable sample size that looks back at all transactions within a 10-day window, specifically around year-end. I'll also cover inventory, checking counts at various locations and testing high-value or slow-moving items for accuracy and potential write-downs as needed.
**Identifying sample and data requirements**

I need to select a sample of items that are flagged as slow-moving or low-turnover. For this, I’ll gather various data, like trial balances, monthly sales details, and inventory listings. Additional info needed includes pick/pack/ship journals, shipping manifests for a 10-day window, sales contracts for complex transactions, and access to count teams. I'll also look into management's inventory reserve policies and any evidence for write-downs. 

Plus, I must address fraud risks, like revenue recognition issues and inventory risks.
**Planning testing and timeline**

I’m set to conduct extended testing for related-party transactions and large customers, as well as review unusual returns after year-end. To stay on track, I'll have the staff start data pulls and sampling today, performing cut-off testing and inventory observations over the next three days. They'll document findings in standardized templates, and I'll escalate any exceptions immediately. I’ll review everything daily and provide updates by the end of the day, requesting manager or partner escalation for any significant issues.
rounds.response: Plan (brief): For revenue cut‑off I will use the provided trial balance and detailed sales-by-month plus shipping/ASN/BOL data to test all sales >$50k and a random sample of 40 transactions (20 recorded in the last 10 days of the year and 20 in the first 10 days of the new year); staff auditor to pull invoice, shipping/packing list/BOL, customer order and any cash receipt/credit memo for each sampled sale and corroborate ship date to determine proper period. For inventory existence/obsolescence I will use the 12/31 inventory listing and location breakdowns to observe year‑end counts at the two largest locations and perform test counts/reconciliations for 5 additional locations, vouching sampled high‑value and slow‑moving SKUs to receiving/shipping records and production schedules; staff to execute count observation, recounts, and populate variance memos for any reconciling items >$5k. Please provide today: shipping manifests/BOLs/ASNs and pick/pack reports for +/-10 days around year‑end, list of large/related‑party customers, physical inventory count schedule and count teams, perpetual movement detail, and management’s inventory reserve policy/aging support and any post‑year‑end returns/credit memos. Heightened risks noted: year‑end premature revenue recognition/side agreements or channel stuffing and risk of overstated/obsolete inventory or management override—we’ll expand testing on large, related‑party, and slow‑moving items and review post‑year‑end returns. To keep on track: staff starts pulls and walkthroughs today, I will review workpapers daily, and I will escalate any exceptions to you immediately so we can resolve before the internal sign‑off deadline.
